summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior stents, diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted for pleuritic chest pain lasting three days. The pain was positional and worse with inspiration, differing from prior myocardial infarctions. Initial evaluation showed normal troponins, no EKG evidence of acute ischemia, and a normal echocardiogram. A nuclear stress test was normal, and imaging ruled out pulmonary embolism and aortic dissection. The clinical picture was consistent with pericarditis. The patient responded well to acetaminophen and symptom management, with no complications. Chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and heart failure were managed with continued medications. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions for pain control, weight monitoring, and cardiology follow-up.
